input.title: Serving a backfill page in the operation index's own order costs 2.5× the load jobs and does not buy cross-scope ordering, because replay regroups by scope anyway

input.description: Measured on a 410-document, 7,056-operation fixture: 817 jobs at 8.6 ops each by document and scope versus 2,016 at 3.5 by ordinal, and 2.64x the wall clock. Replay reduces scope by scope.

metadata.reason: Extracted from docs/updateoutbox-scope-ordering.md at v6.2.2-dev.74 — 'What the fix is, and what it is not': the two counts, the measurement table, and 'The cycle that surfaced while trying the index order'
Records why the tempting fix for that bug was rejected and what was shipped instead

input.content:
The obvious fix for the scope-ordering inversion was to drop the sort and serve each page in the index's ordinal order. It was tried and rejected on two counts.

**It costs a factor of 2.5 in load jobs.** Measured against the hub-spoke fixture (410 documents, 7,056 operations, 407 documents carrying exactly two scopes):

| batching | load jobs | operations per job |
| --- | --- | --- |
| by (document, scope) | 817 | 8.6 |
| by (document, ordinal) | 2,016 | 3.5 |

Convergence time tracked that ratio almost exactly — 2.47× the jobs for 2.64× the wall clock — so the cost is per-job overhead, not per-operation work. On CI it took the 3-spoke leg past its 300 s cap and then took Postgres down with it.

**It does not buy the ordering it appears to buy.** Delivery order is not what decides the order a document's scopes are applied in: `replayDocument` replays `Object.values(operations).flatMap(...)` — scope by scope, with no cross-scope sort — so given `global@1000, local@2000, global@3000, local@4000` it applies `global@1000, global@3000, local@2000, local@4000`. The one place operations from different streams are ordered by timestamp, `mergeByPosition`/`comparePositions`, is reached only from the auth walk and does not feed state derivation. So an `UPGRADE_DOCUMENT` is **not** applied at the position its timestamp implies relative to other scopes today, whatever order it is delivered in. If that semantics is wanted it belongs in replay, and batching per document rather than per (document, scope) is the enabler — 410 jobs on the fixture against 817.

A related defect surfaced while trying the index order and is reachable on `main`: `consolidateSyncOperations` merged **every** SyncOperation sharing a `(documentId, scope, branch)` wherever it sat in the chain, so an alternating chain `j1 document → j2 auth → j3 document → j4 auth` collapsed into `j1 → [j2]` and `j2 → [j1]`, which `validateBatchStructure` rejects for the whole batch. Merging only contiguous runs keeps the chain linear.

_Source: docs/updateoutbox-scope-ordering.md (Powerhouse v6.2.2-dev.74)._
